title: Temple of Dendur, Nubia

terrainReference.basis: Current independent surface at the archaeological coordinate. The modern DEM cannot recover the inundated 1874 ground elevation.

mapIdentity.provider: Harrell historical site gazetteer and Gau’s measured west-bank period survey.
mapIdentity.scope: The approximate archaeological gazetteer point anchors the original Nubian temple. Gau surveyed the footprint and west-bank site in 1819 and Blackman gave dimensions in 1911. Modern Lake Nasser covers the area, so the stand-alone scene restores only the local relative levels shown in the historical evidence.

note: The measured Gau plates and the exact published 1874 Bridgman image establish the broad sandstone platform, east-facing gateway and the lowered rock bank. Teynard’s pre-dam photograph supplies the surviving stone silhouettes and slope.
